title: Direction Signs: Colour by Road Type
whatItIs: Direction signs are colour-coded, so you can tell at a glance what type of road they lead to.
keyFacts: Blue backgrounds are used on motorways.
Green backgrounds are used on primary routes.
White backgrounds with a black border are used on other (non-primary and local) routes.
Brown signs point to tourist attractions and facilities.
A blue panel on a green or white sign shows a route to a motorway.

visual.caption: The colour tells you the type of road

items.title: Green
items.text: Primary routes: the main roads linking towns and cities.

onTheTest.question: What colour are direction signs on primary routes?
onTheTest.why: Green is for primary routes, blue for motorways, white for other roads and brown for tourist destinations.

traps: A blue panel on a green sign points to a motorway: the road you're on isn't a motorway yet.
Brown signs are for tourist places, not a type of road.
Don't mix up blue direction signs (motorways) with blue circles (orders).
